summary: List all pairs of elements with the minimum absolute difference.
mainInsight: After sorting, the minimum difference is always between adjacent elements. Do one pass to find the minimum adjacent difference and a second pass (or the same pass with reset) to collect all adjacent pairs with that difference.

approaches.name: Sort and scan adjacent pairs
approaches.summary: Find min diff, then collect pairs.

commonMistakes: Reporting only the first minimum pair
Not resetting the list on finding a smaller gap

promptVariants: Which technique solves this problem, and what in the statement or constraints points to it?

cards.answer: Sort, then the minimum difference is between adjacent elements: scan adjacent pairs to find it and collect them. Clue: The smallest gap between values always lies between neighbours in sorted order, and the pairs have to be listed in ascending order anyway, so sort and scan adjacent elements.
keyPoints: The smallest gap between values always lies between neighbours in sorted order, and the pairs have to be listed in ascending order anyway, so sort and scan adjacent elements.
cards.explanation: In sorted order any pair further apart has a gap at least as large as the gaps in between, so only neighbours matter.

promptVariants: Why does sorting reduce the problem to adjacent elements?
Which pairs can have the minimum difference?
options: In sorted order the closest elements are neighbours
The largest and smallest elements are always the closest
Equal elements always come at the end
The median pair always has the minimum gap
cards.answer: In sorted order the closest elements are neighbours
cards.explanation: Any non-adjacent pair has a larger gap than the pairs between them.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Equal elements always come at the end: Sorting does not place equals at the end.
incorrectOptionExplanations.The median pair always has the minimum g: The gap is unrelated to the median.

promptVariants: Why can't a non-adjacent pair have the minimum difference unless some adjacent pair also does?
How do you collect all minimal pairs?
cards.answer: If a < b < c in sorted order then c - a > b - a and c - a > c - b, so a non-adjacent pair is strictly farther than its inner adjacent pairs (equal only with duplicates, which are adjacent). Therefore it suffices to track the minimum adjacent gap and list every adjacent pair achieving it.
cards.explanation: Reset the result list when a smaller gap is found.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: The sorted copy and the output pairs (O(log n) auxiliary).

options: [[3, 5]]: only the first pair is reported
cards.explanation: Sorted, the neighbours differ by 2 each time, so all three adjacent pairs are reported in ascending order.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[[3, 9]]: the extremes are the closest: The extremes are the farthest apart, not the closest.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[[3, 5]]: only the first pair is reporte: Every pair with the minimum difference must be reported, not just the first.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[[3, 7], [5, 9]]: pairs with a differenc: The minimum difference is 2, so pairs 4 apart are not part of the answer.
